# CoreML

**Area:** [Imaging, photos & ML](../COVERAGE.md#ml) · **Apple:** [CoreML](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/coreml) · **Issues:** [`area:ml`](https://github.com/kolabs-dev/isim/issues?q=is%3Aissue+is%3Aopen+label%3Aarea%3Aml)

## How isim implements it

- **Adapted:** isim parses the model specification itself and runs GLM models only. Xcode-compiled `.mlmodelc` is undocumented.

## API

| API / feature | Status | iOS | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Core ML data API (`MLMultiArray`, `MLFeatureValue`, `MLDictionaryFeatureProvider`, `MLArrayBatchProvider`, `MLModelConfiguration`, `MLModelDescription`) | ✅ | ≤17 | tested (shapes, strides, subscripts, feature values) |
| Core ML models in projects (`.mlmodel`, `.mlpackage`; Xcode's generated model classes) | ✅ | ≤17 | adapted: `isim build` compiles each model in Compile Sources (or a synchronized folder) into `<Name>.mlmodelc` in the app with isim's format (the spec, what `MLModel(contentsOf:)` loads; a package's root model from its `Manifest.json`) instead of Apple's undocumented one, and generates Xcode's Swift classes from the model's description: `<Name>Input` / `<Name>Output` (`MLFeatureProvider`, a property per feature: Int64, Double, String, CVPixelBuffer, MLMultiArray, dictionaries, MLSequence; optional inputs), `<Name>` (`init(configuration:)`, `init(contentsOf:configuration:)`, `load(configuration:)` async and with a completion handler, `urlOfModelInThisBundle`, `prediction(input:)`, `prediction(<inputs>:)`, `predictions(inputs:options:)`); `COREML_CODEGEN_LANGUAGE = None` turns generation off. `import CoreML` re-exports Foundation, as Apple's does (the generated classes use URL and Bundle). Not generated: Objective-C model classes (isim's Core ML has no Objective-C interface yet). What a model can predict is the next row. Tested (HelloCoreMLModels: test_generated_model_classes, test_coreml_models) |
| Core ML `MLModel` loading and prediction | 🟡 | ≤17 | adapted: Apple's compiled `.mlmodelc` format is undocumented and needs Apple's runtime, so Xcode-compiled models fail to load with a clear error (tested); `MLModel.compileModel(at:)` turns a `.mlmodel` spec into an isim `.mlmodelc`; descriptions are read for every model type (with `stateDescriptionsByName`); predictions run for GLM regressors/classifiers, tree ensembles and neural networks (next rows); ML programs and pipelines fail with a clear error (tested) |
| Core ML tree ensembles (`treeEnsembleRegressor`, `treeEnsembleClassifier`) | ✅ | ≤17 | adapted: isim evaluates the spec's trees on the CPU (branch modes, missing values, base values, softmax / logistic post-transforms, class labels and probabilities). Tested (CoreMLTest: test_coreml_runtime) |
| Core ML neural networks (`neuralNetwork`, `neuralNetworkRegressor`, `neuralNetworkClassifier`) and `MLCustomLayer` | 🟡 | ≤17 | adapted: isim runs the network on the CPU, layer by layer: inner product, activations (linear, ReLU, leaky / thresholded ReLU, tanh, scaled tanh, sigmoid, hard sigmoid, ELU, softsign, softplus), batch norm, softmax, add, multiply, concat, reshape, flatten, and custom layers (the app's `MLCustomLayer` class, found by `className`); float32 / float16 / raw weights. Other layer types (convolution, pooling, recurrent, …) fail with an error naming the layer. Tested (CoreMLTest) |
| `MLShapedArray`, `MLShapedArraySlice`, `MLShapedArrayProtocol`, `MLShapedArrayScalar` | ✅ | ≤17 | adapted (pure Swift): shapes, strides, scalar / index / range subscripts, reshape, expand / squeeze, transpose, concatenation, identity and random arrays, Codable, conversion to and from `MLMultiArray` and `MLFeatureValue`. Tested (CoreMLTest) |
| `MLState`, `MLModel.makeState()`, `prediction(from:using:options:)` | ✅ | 18.0 | adapted: state buffers come from the model description's state features and persist between predictions; `withMultiArray(for:)` reads and writes them. Tested (CoreMLTest) |
| `MLTensor`, `MLTensorScalar`, `MLTensorRangeExpression` | ✅ | 18.0 | adapted: an eager CPU tensor (Double storage): creation, broadcasting arithmetic, comparisons, reductions, matmul, shape operations, gather / replacing, padding, resizing, top-k, subscripts, seeded random; `shapedArray(of:)` materialises it. Tested (CoreMLTest) |
| `MLComputeDevice`, `MLCPUComputeDevice`, `MLGPUComputeDevice`, `MLNeuralEngineComputeDevice`, `MLComputePlan`, `MLModelStructure` | ✅ | ≤17 | adapted: isim computes on the CPU only, so `MLModel.availableComputeDevices` and `MLComputeDevice.allComputeDevices` list the CPU; `MLComputePlan.load` describes the model's structure (neural network layers, program or pipeline) with every layer on the CPU and no cost estimate. Tested (CoreMLTest) |
| `MLUpdateTask`, `MLUpdateContext`, `MLUpdateProgressHandlers`, `MLParameterKey`, `MLMetricKey` | 🟡 | ≤17 | stub: the types exist so apps compile; on-device training is not implemented and creating an `MLUpdateTask` throws an `.update` error. Tested (CoreMLTest) |
| Types not yet in isim (iOS 17 and earlier) | ❌ | ≤17 | not implemented, found by the 2026-10 sweep: `MLCustomModel`, `MLModelAsset`, `MLTask` (3 types; with their members under "Not yet in isim") |
| Types not yet in isim (iOS 18) | ❌ | 18.0 | not implemented, found by the 2026-10 sweep: `MLComputePolicy`, `MLSendableFeatureValue`, `MLStateConstraint` (3 types; with their members under "Not yet in isim") |
